message.content: SELECT category_id, COUNT(*) AS tickets FROM support_tickets GROUP BY category_id ORDER BY tickets DESC, category_id ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 100;
message.reasoning_content:
The user wants: count tickets grouped by category_id that actually appear in support_tickets. Only categories with tickets. Output category_id and ticket count.

Rules: "按客服工单中实际出现的category_id分类编号统计各分类的工单数" — they ask for category_id (编号), not name. So use support_tickets.category_id, count tickets (COUNT(DISTINCT ticket_id) or COUNT(*) since ticket_id is PK, single table no dup). Simply COUNT(*).

Order? "统计各分类的工单数" — no order specified. Default maybe ORDER BY count desc. Add LIMIT.

Rule 8: 明确名称/编号/编码/输出列优先 — they ask category_id 编号. Don't join tiket_categories for name.

No filter. SQL:

SELECT category_id, COUNT(*) AS tickets FROM support_tickets GROUP BY category_id ORDER BY tickets DESC LIMIT 100;

Need LIMIT since GROUP BY present. Use LIMIT 100.

Should category_id be NULL? "实际出现" — includes NULL? Probably exclude NULL... hmm. NULL category_id is a value appeared? Default rules: 普通列表保留未知. Keep NULL. But ORDER BY tickets DESC then NULL... fine.

Maybe order by count desc, category_id asc tie-break.
